ehrenfest_0.m: Damn it, kid! Watch your step. You almost knocked me over!
r: Sorry, I am in a hurry.
Watch my step? You'd better watch your tongue!

ehrenfest_10b.m: Hah! I seriously doubt they are here just for that.
r: Are you accusing the great soldiers of Feygard of anything? I'd better leave.

ehrenfest_11.m: Hello again my little friend. We'll be safe from prying ears here.
r: Care to explain your reasons for stalking me?

ehrenfest_12.m: I only saw you by chance. Please, let me explain what happened.

ehrenfest_13a.m: I arrived here several weeks ago for no particularly interesting reason. I am part of a family of explorers and travelers, and the story of a ruined tunnel infested by dangerous beasts was something I wanted to see with my own eyes.

ehrenfest_14.m: The rumors were true. Those gornauds are not natural creatures. They gave me a really hard time at first.

ehrenfest_15.m: I managed to reach the other entrance of the tunnel, but with no potions or fresh food I thought it was the end. Luckily, a guy called Lorn rescued me and brought me here.
r: That name seems familiar to me, somehow.

ehrenfest_16.m: Due to my exhaustion, I rested in bed for days. I could hear the constant noise of the workers chatting, toasting with their mead jugs...

ehrenfest_17.m: But the day I got up, completely recovered, the first thing I noticed was precisely the absence of those noises. The rooms next to me were dirty and empty. No one was in the dining room. The mine entrance was closed.

ehrenfest_17a.m: [He seems to be completely absorbed by his own monologue]

ehrenfest_18.m: Arghest, the only man left here, pointed me towards Prim, so I decided to go and ask for my savior. Lamentably, he was no longer there.

ehrenfest_19.m: Some villagers said he and his patrol crew had left three days ago in search of a couple that climbed up the mountain. So I went to the local shop, I got some supplies and...

r: As I said, I don't have time to talk. I need to report something important.
Nothing of your concern. I must go inside.
I have discovered something suspicious inside the mountain.

ehrenfest_1b.m: Not only blind but bad-mannered too! You remind me of myself when I was younger. I was not blind, though, ha ha ha!

ehrenfest_1b2.m: I'll let it go. But tell me, what is it that you find so urgent?
r: I don't trust you with something this important, so nothing.
I have information related to recent disappearances.
Sorry, it's important, so I must go.

ehrenfest_20a.m: I suppose, if you want to call it that.

ehrenfest_20b.m: Are you gonna stop interrupting me?
r: If that makes you finish sooner...

ehrenfest_21.m: Well. After nearly two days of restless searching, I figured they may have already returned, so I started to climb down.

ehrenfest_22.m: I fell off a cliff on a narrow path on the mountain side and ended up at the same plateau you climbed up to, where the corpse was. I could not believe what I was seeing.

ehrenfest_23.m: Lorn lay next to me, just a few steps away. His armor was entirely covered in blood, flowing slowly to the ground out of his body.

ehrenfest_24a.m: There was a campfire, yes. Now that I think about it, it could have belonged either to the couple or to the patrol crew.

ehrenfest_24b.m: I didn't dare to go down the hole...
r: Was Lorn dead when you found him?
I found some dead bodies inside.

ehrenfest_24c.m: Almost... I took his armor off. His injuries were severe. I tried to cure him using my potions but they weren't strong enough. He died, failing to express his final thoughts in words.

ehrenfest_24c2.m: But everything he couldn't say with words was said by the terrified glance he threw at that dark hole, just before his last breath.

ehrenfest_25a.m: Yes, I was about to ask you... Continue.
r: The corpses were covered by cobwebs, but I could see signs of torture.

ehrenfest_25b.m: Anything more you can tell me about that place?
r: Give me some time to remember.
The corpses were covered by cobwebs. They were probably tortured.

ehrenfest_26a.m: Tortured, you say? That makes no sense!
r: I took some ropes to prove what I saw to the guards...
Yes, look at this blood-stained rope.
Yes, look at this blood-stained rope... Oh, I seem to have lost it. Just a second, I'll go and find it.

ehrenfest_27b.m: Just after witnessing my savior's death, I ran away and came back to the village.
r: Did you tell the guards what you saw?
Shame on you! You should have buried him at least.

ehrenfest_28a.m: I tried, but they considered it an accident. My constant babbling did not help...
r: Why did the guards not bury their partner?

ehrenfest_28b.m: You are honestly right, but it's too late to go back...
r: You didn't bury him, but why didn't the guards either?

ehrenfest_29a.m: Strange, isn't it? Really, they didn't seem to care about Lorn, or the other missing people. It was all the monsters' fault and that's all.
r: There's something too shady in all of this.
Guards, lazy as hell in every place I go.

ehrenfest_29b.m: [Ehrenfest stays quiet with his head down]
r: So ... Why didn't the guards bring Lorn's remains to the village?

ehrenfest_2a.m: I see. But keep in mind that no one inside there will pay attention to you, whatever you say.

ehrenfest_2b2.m: Look, I personally don't think that telling the guards is a good choice.

ehrenfest_30a.m: Yes. And that's why I need your help.
r: You should give me a reward just for listening to this tripe.

ehrenfest_30b.m: Sometimes, heh. But still, something doesn't fit.
r: Indeed. There's something shady in all of this.

ehrenfest_30c.m: Now that everything is told, let's find some answers.

ehrenfest_31a.m: We must gather information. I am convinced Lorn's death has to do with what you saw down the hole.

ehrenfest_31b.m: Okay, okay. Let's take a break. We'll talk later.
r: Do you have anything to trade?

ehrenfest_32a.m: You will have to talk to the villagers of Prim. We have to find out what happened to Lorn's partners, about whom we know nothing yet.
r: Sounds boring, but I'll do it.

ehrenfest_33a.m: I will ask in the inn about the missing couple that Lorn and his partners followed.
r: I'd complain, but I prefer not to hear your explanation.

ehrenfest_33b.m: Excellent. Let's meet again later, best of luck.

r: You lied to me. There wasn't any missing couple.

ehrenfest_35a.m: Don't give up. We'll eventually get some answers.

ehrenfest_35b.m: You are right, but I didn't lie.
r: How is it not a lie?

ehrenfest_36.m: Remember while you were asking for Lorn, I asked some villagers precisely about that missing couple.
r: I'm not going to hear your stories anymore.
What I remember is you, telling me about that missing couple.
Again, you did. I cannot trust you.
I can't be sure of that.

ehrenfest_38a.m: I won't try to convince you. Now you must decide whether to help me or not. I won't ask twice, so make your choice wisely.
r: I don't trust you. I will find my own way to solve this.
I'll think about it. See you soon.
OK, I will help you. Let's solve this once for all.

ehrenfest_39a.m:
I see...Good luck, you'll need it.

[Ehrenfest walks slowly out of the room]
r: You're still being shady, huh. Goodbye.

ehrenfest_39b.m: Excellent. Let's share what we found out then.
r: You're already aware of my information.

ehrenfest_39c.m: It's time to share what we've discovered.
r: You are already aware of my information.

ehrenfest_3a.m: OK, kid. Do it, and I'll wait here for your return, heh. By the way, my name is Ehrenfest.

ehrenfest_3b.m: This is not a good place to talk about this. But trust me, there is much at stake and Prim's situation is only going to get worse. Let me introduce myself. My name is Ehrenfest, and...

ehrenfest_4.m: *looks nervous*  I told you. Something big is about to happen. I believe it is somehow related to what you've seen up in the mountain.
r: How did they reach this place?
How do you know what I've seen?

ehrenfest_41a.m: Then, it seems I've been the lucky one this time.

ehrenfest_41b.m: Both villagers and guards seemed pretty uneasy when I asked about the Feygard soldiers' presence.

r: Yes. Please, tell me what you've discovered.

ehrenfest_42.m: I strongly believe they're related to the disappearings.
r: That has to be taken with a grain of salt.

ehrenfest_43.m: Put it this way. A weakened Prim will be easier to control. Although Lord Geomyr theoretically reigns over the whole land, his influence has its limits, as I'm sure you know well. Isolated regions like Prim have considerable independence.

ehrenfest_44.m: It is well known there is an ancient chamber dedicated to worship of the Shadow, which is probably Lord Geomyr's most powerful threat.

ehrenfest_45a.m: That Feygard general said he was gonna climb up the mountain. We should follow him up to Blackwater Settlement and stop him.
r: Stop him? You mean to kill him?
I'd love to get rid of that Feygard scum.

ehrenfest_45b.m: This is our best bet. I think we'd have to act before it's too late.

r: Never mind, killing him is the safest choice.

ehrenfest_46b.m: Excellent, excellent! I will lead the way, meet me at Blackwater Settlement. Beware of the monsters.
r: Same to you, those scared monsters will make way to me.

ehrenfest_47.m: Are you crazy or something? He would never talk to commoners like us!
r: We will never know if we don't try.
You're right. It'll be better to get rid of him as soon as possible.
You're the insane guy here, thinking we can beat a group of elite trained soldiers.

ehrenfest_48.m: I think you need some time to think about it.

ehrenfest_49.m: Hmm... $playername, I wonder how your brother Andor would react if he knew I had to kill you.
r: What do you know about him?!
So you're the guy that Lodar told me about.
I won't hear your lies. I'll finish you right here.

ehrenfest_50a.m:
If only you were stronger...Maybe I could convince you to join us, [cough] but I have to admit my plan was blaming you for Ortholion's death.

You know, we're tired of you asking questions here and there, [cough] [cough].

ehrenfest_50b.m: Lodar, right. He sins of double morality! His poisons killed hundreds, but he prefers to hide in that dirty forest and escape any responsibility like a retired farmer.

ehrenfest_50c.m:
No you won't, sorry. 

My mission is done here. It was done weeks ago, but I...Someone decided I should stay and draw Feygard's attention here.

ehrenfest_51.m: Don't look at me that way, kid...[laughs]. This is too complicated for a young mind.

ehrenfest_52.m:
How tetchy! The guards I tortured eventually understood my words... 

Maybe you should try that orangish substance too.

ehrenfest_53.m:
Ehrenfest jumps off the cliff, sinking in the dark streams, leaving you in the middle of a word.

You soon begin to hear steps. Someone's coming - maybe the Feygard reinforcements?

ehrenfest_5a.m: I assume the same way you did.

ehrenfest_5b.m:
I've seen you climbing up the mountainside and going down the hole, of course!

I was waiting for your return.
r: All of this is getting too shady. I'd better leave.

ehrenfest_6a.m: Look, this is not a safe place to talk. Meet me in the Elm mine, west of here, OK?
r: I hope this won't get any shadier.

ehrenfest_6b.m: Do whatever you want, youngster. But two minds sometimes work better than one, and four eyes better than two...

ehrenfest_7a.m: OK, I'll be waiting for you there.

ehrenfest_7b.m: Excellent. Try not to raise suspicions.

r: No luck, but I heard a tense conversation between a Feygard general and one of the patrol captains.

ehrenfest_9.m: I did see that general leaving. Now his henchmen are patrolling the village entrance.
r: They are up to no good.
It's good to see they are protecting the villagers.

ehrenfest_conversation_1a.m: You and Ehrenfest are startled, and step aside. Three men with Feygard insignia leave the hall. You remain silent as they pass.

ehrenfest_conversation_2.m: I will say it only once. No taverns, no exploring, no drama with those untrained Prim guards. And for the glory of our homeland, don't pursue any injured monster.

ehrenfest_conversation_3.m: I have a bad feeling about all this. These villagers might be hiding something. Tell the mountain scouts to wait for me at the tunnel entrance. They will escort me up to Blackwater Settlement.

ehrenfest_conversation_4a.m: The three men continue on their way out of the village, completely ignoring your presence.

omi2_fix_ehrenfest_53.m: You are wrong. I'm not here, just an illusion.

ortholion_1.m: Look, I don't have time for you, but I don't kill kids, not yet. So step aside.
r: I'm here to inform you about Ehrenfest. He's probably behind some disappearances in Prim.

ortholion_2b.m: You mean that weakling is responsible of those missing people from Prim of whom I've been recently informed?
r: Weakling? Haven't you seen how he escaped?

ortholion_3b.m: Nothing impressive. Loyal followers of the Shadow have their tricks, just as I have my own.
r: The Shadow? Do you believe in that?
Hope those tricks are better than your chasing abilities.

ortholion_3b2.m: There's definitely something off with him. Another Shadow fanatic to get rid of, tsch.
r: Shadow fanatic? Do you know him?

ortholion_4a.m: Hmm...Maybe. You came up this far after all. Go warn my soldiers. They are settled in the tunnel entrance, south of Prim.
r: This is getting too complicated. I'd better leave.
I bet they'll pay attention to a kid like me, right?

ortholion_4b.m: [Laughs quietly] Only simple minds would see things as black or white. Whether I believe or not, people do, and we in Feygard keep that in mind.
r: OK. Now that you're aware of the situation, I'd better leave.
What about "I don't have time to..."?

ortholion_4c.m: I have no time for this absurd talk. I must be sure this guy's road ends in the Elm mine.

ortholion_4d.m: No. But it's quite obvious by the way he accused me.
r: And what will you do, General Slowness?
Well, this is not really my problem. Bye.

ortholion_5a.m: Not so fast. Seeing that you reached this place but my scouts couldn't, I think you will be of use.
r: What if I don't want to help you?

ortholion_6a.m: Then I'll officially accuse you of betrayal and attempted murder against a Feygard general. I'll bring you to Feygard and you will never see your family again.
r: How dare you?! Prepare to die!

ortholion_6b.m: Take this, and show it to the soldiers stationed near the mining tunnel entrance. Tell them I went to the Elm mine.

ortholion_7a.m:
[The general effortlessly subdues you, and begins to laugh] 

Look, take this signet. With this, my soldiers stationed outside the mining tunnel entrance will believe your words. Tell them I went to the Elm mine.
r: OK, OK. I will but please don't hurt me anymore.

ortholion_8a.m: Are you still here?! Go, go now!
r: Someday you will regret your manners...

ortholion_conversation2_1.m: Ehrenfest, you have come this far just to get rid of me...
r: Ehrenfest, here I am to help you.
Ortholion, beware! He is a dangerous liar!

ortholion_conversation2_2a.m: The crimes you have commited must be punished!

ortholion_conversation2_2b.m: I hoped someone else would take the blame for this. But don't worry, soon we shall be unstoppable.
r: Do you always talk this much, liar?

ortholion_conversation2_3a.m:
Hmmm... What crimes, evil creature?

You even dared to think you had a chance to trick a general of glorious Feygard?!

ortholion_conversation2_3b.m: [unsheathes his sword] Well, enough talk. I won't ignore your threats, evil creature.
r: Ehrenfest, you have many things to explain!

ortholion_conversation2_4a.m:
I'm... [stares at you] 

$playername! It's time to end with all of this!
r: Right! Ortholion must pay for killing innocent people from Prim!

ortholion_conversation2_4b.m:
[People from the tavern start looking at the place where Ortholion and Ehrenfest are about to have a fight]

[looks around] No...Not yet. Argh! You kid, betrayer! You are about to discover how wrongly you have chosen!

ortholion_conversation2_5a.m: A kid? You come with a kid accusing me of something I never heard about?

ortholion_conversation2_5a2.m: General Ortholion ignores you and continues to speak to Ehrenfest.

ortholion_conversation2_5b.m:
[The general tries to land a strike on Ehrenfest, but he just cuts a piece of his cloak. Ehrenfest is gone]

Hmpf...
r: I thought Feygard generals were faster swinging their blades.

ortholion_conversation2_6a.m: Ehrenfest, you have bothered me more than I am willing to abide. Blackwater Settlement guards will take care of you.
r: Those guards are no match for...

ortholion_conversation2_6a2.m: Just before starting to launch an attack, General Ortholion moves and disarms you with a single blow.

ortholion_conversation2_7a.m:
Bah! This is enough. $playername. Weren't you so strong? Pathetic.

You only had to distract him and take the blame!
r: Hah. I always knew you were far too shady to be an honest man.

ortholion_conversation2_8a.m:
Ortholion! How much is your life worth? How many people?

Prove the honor of your glorious land. Come face me alone! No guards, no witnesses.

[Ehrenfest leaps unnaturally high, passing above you, and disappears in the blink of an eye]

bwm72_beginning.6: Conversation with Ehrenfest starts before Ortholion appears.
bwm72_beginning.7: Conversation with Ehrenfest starts after Ortholion leaves.
bwm72_beginning.8: Ehrenfest notices your presence in the mine and calls you.
bwm72_beginning.35: Bad opinion from Ortholion's remaining henchman

andor.1: My father Mikhail says that Andor has not been home since yesterday. I should go look for him in the village.
andor.10: Leonid tells me that he saw Andor talking to Gruil. I should go ask Gruil if he knows more.
andor.20: Gruil wants me to bring him a poison gland. Then he might talk more. He tells me that some poisonous snakes have such a gland.
andor.30: Gruil tells me that Andor was looking for someone called Umar. I should go ask his friend Gaela in Fallhaven to the east.
andor.40: I talked to Gaela in Fallhaven. He tells me to go see Bucus and ask about the Thieves' Guild.
andor.50: Bucus has allowed me to enter the hatch in the derelict house in Fallhaven. I should go talk to Umar.
andor.51: Umar in the Fallhaven Thieves' Guild recognized me, but must have me confused with Andor. Apparently, Andor has been to see him.
andor.55: Umar told me that Andor went to see a potion maker called Lodar. I should search for his hideaway.
andor.61: I heard a story in Loneford, where it seemed like Andor had been in Loneford, and that he might have had something to do with the illness that the people are suffering from there. I am not sure if it actually was Andor. If it was Andor, why would he have made the people of Loneford ill?
andor.62: Andor might have gone to do some business with a rich man in Brimhaven after he left Loneford.
andor.65: It looks like Andor was involved in the destruction of the Brimhaven dam.
andor.70: I have found the potion-maker Lodar, and heard his story about Andor. Andor went to visit Lodar in his hideaway to get a sample of something called Narwood extract. Lodar happened to notice that there was someone travelling together with Andor, that hid among the trees and did not seem to want Lodar to spot him.
andor.71: Shortly after Andor and the person he was travelling with had left, strange things started to happen in the woods around Lodar's hideaway, and Lodar himself seemed to be affected by it somehow. Lodar believes that something disturbed the tomb below his cabin, and awoke the Hira'zinn.
andor.72: Since I helped Lodar defeat the Hira'zinn, he promised to help me in return. He gave me a piece of paper that should allow me to enter the Valanyr temple of the Shadow in Nor City. He told me to seek out lady Lydalon in the temple for further assistance.
andor.80: All clues so far as to where Andor went point to Nor City. I should travel to Nor City by following the Duleian road to the southeast and look for more clues there.
andor.85: Andor may have been in Stoutford.
andor.86: Andor had something to do with the demon under the church in Stoutford.
andor.90: At Castle Guynmart I learned from Steward Unkorh that some time ago Andor was also there as a guest.
andor.92: Unkorh gave me the bonemeal potion box that Andor had given him for safekeeping.
andor.100: While exploring the town of Sullengard, I so happened to stumble upon my mother and my aunt to whom I have never met. Mother has insisted that I go home so we can talk.
andor.110: After talking with mother back at home, she and I tried to brainstorm about where Andor could be. She reminded me about Andor's friend Stanwick who lives in Brightport. We agreed that going to talk to him might be the next logical thing to do.
andor.120: In the dungeons of Laeroth manor, Kotheses, the torturer, mentioned that he had taught Andor the basics of torturing.
andor.125: Vaelric confirmed that Andor visited him recently. Andor sought to learn Vaelric's skills and left quickly, clutching what he came for. His actions raise more questions about his intentions.
andor.126: In Brightport, I was finally able to meet Stanwick, but due to his hazy memory, he was not able to help me learn anything about the whereabouts of Andor.
andor.127: Regaining his peace of mind after I helped him, Stanwick said he'll tell me more about Andor, once he gathers his thoughts.
andor.128: Stanwick gave me a signet ring that I should show to his father. Jorwick, in Nor City.
andor.130: Andor was trying to find out from Seraphina about terrible monsters in the hideout near the place with the larval burrowers.
andor.131: Elysa in the Brightport's thieves guild told me that Andor has bought a map to the sewers of Feygard.
andor.132: While investigating the Brightport theft I learned from Bryma that Andor was the one who stole the important document, and brought it to her in exchange for her alchemy knowledge.
andor.140: I saw Andor in the mountains of Galmore. We were able to exchange a few words before he disappeared again.
andor.145: I met Andor on the road to Feygard, where he was buying food from Rosmara. He disappeared again.
andor.147: I met Andor on the road to Nor City, where he was buying supplies from Alynndir. He disappeared again.
andor.910: I decided to settle down on the top of Mt. Galmore. For this I needed to find a rich and discreet man to rebuild the ruins according to my wishes. Andor will now have to go and find himself.
andor.912: The construction contract for my new home was completed. I was curious to see what it would look like.
andor.914: I visited my new residence on the top of Mt. Galmore. There I would help the people of Dhayavar as a hero and protect them from villains. Or would I become a villain myself? We'll see.
andor.999: [Quest is not completable at this time.]

Omi2_bwm1.5: Down in a hole, in the mountain side near Prim, I found signs of a heinous torture. At least three corpses were there. I felt the urge to get out of there as fast as I could and immediately report what I found to someone in the village.
Omi2_bwm1.6: A mysterious looking guy suddenly appeared in my way when I was headed to report to the guards. He has recommended that I should not tell them anything.
Omi2_bwm1.7: I ignored the advice of the strange guy that I almost stumbled over. I must see some guards.
Omi2_bwm1.8: Somehow, a Feygard general and his men reached Prim. They are kind of extorting the people in charge to get full control of Elm mine.
Omi2_bwm1.9: The man in charge is not willing to listen to me. He says he has more important things to deal with. Maybe the guy I met earlier was right.
Omi2_bwm1.10: A Feygard general and two of his henchmen appeared. What are they up to?
Omi2_bwm1.11: Ehrenfest is uneasy. He said we must meet in Elm mine, west of prim. We should talk no more about this inside the village.
Omi2_bwm1.15: Ehrenfest told me his story, and why he knew about what I saw on the mountain side, but he didn't dare to go down the hole.
Omi2_bwm1.16: I explained to Ehrenfest the horrible scene, and showed him proof of the torture. Poor guys...
Omi2_bwm1.20: I must ask the villagers about Lorn and his partners, maybe I can gather some useful information from the common gossip.
Omi2_bwm1.21: It seems Lorn was a regular client of the tavern. I should ask there.
Omi2_bwm1.22: One of the tavern regulars, possibly Lorn's old partner Jern, does not believe that Lorn's death was an accident, maintaining Lorn had been climbing the mountains for longer than he could remember. However, he does not feel comfortable to continue the conversation.
Omi2_bwm1.23: Lorn's old partner asked me to bring a large bottle of cool water from the streams that are down the hole east of Prim. I bet it is the same hole I've been down earlier.
Omi2_bwm1.24: I've collected enough water. Time to leave this dark place.
Omi2_bwm1.25: I brought the cold water to Lorn's old partner. He seems to be better, and is less intoxicated.
Omi2_bwm1.30: Jern doesn't know anything about a missing couple. How can a member of Lorn's crew ignore the mission of his group? Again, something does not fit. I should visit Ehrenfest again.
Omi2_bwm1.31: I decided to solve this situation myself, as Ehrenfest proved not to be trustworthy enough.
Omi2_bwm1.32: Despite Ehrenfest's ostensible lies, I decided to give him a second chance.
Omi2_bwm1.33: It's settled. Ehrenfest and I will reach Blackwater Settlement and stop General Ortholion's evil plan.
Omi2_bwm1.34: I've found a severely wounded woman inside a mountain cabin. She claims to have been suddenly attacked by a group of wyrms. Ortholion and the other scout left her resting and departed to Blackwater Settlement.
Omi2_bwm1.35: I killed the mountain scout that was taking refuge in the old cabin up in the mountain.
Omi2_bwm1.36: I talked again with Jern. Maybe the guards will be more reasonable if he leads the conversation instead of me.
Omi2_bwm1.40: It seems Ehrenfest lied to me more than once. He's probably connected with the missing people and Lorn's death. I must find General Ortholion and warn him about Ehrenfest.
Omi2_bwm1.41: One of the general's henchmen attacked me without provocation. There was something wrong with her. Better hurry up and meet with the Feygard general.
Omi2_bwm1.45: Ehrenfest revealed his true intentions, but fled before getting surrounded. He told me he will be waiting for General Ortholion in the Elm mine.
Omi2_bwm1.46: After a brief conversation with the general, he left Blackwater settlement in a rush to reach Elm mine. He seemed really worried about the mine, so he asked me to warn his soldiers, settled south of Prim.
Omi2_bwm1.47: I reported to the general's henchmen about his plans. Now, I should hurry to the Elm mine.
Omi2_bwm1.48: Once in the mine I saw corpses and collapsed tunnels. I tried to go another way and reached some more tunnels. Fortunately, they were not collapsed, but there was something strange there that scared even the venomfangs. Something evil.
Omi2_bwm1.49: One of the unexploited areas of the mine had a walled up passage and lots of those strange glowing gems. They seem to consume living beings to grow and bring life to inanimated things or corpses. I must be very careful.
Omi2_bwm1.50: It was true! That strange glowing material is alive. I should be extremely cautious; it seems to be able to engulf living beings. I found the last of Ortholion's henchman alive. He has gone back to search for reinforcements. I hope they are better than those who dared to enter here.
Omi2_bwm1.51: I ended up trapped on a one-way path deep in a cavern below the Elm mine. General Ortholion is blocking the only way to escape for Ehrenfest. This is his end.
Omi2_bwm1.52: Ehrenfest reversed the situation using some kind of magic, seemingly unknown even to himself.
Omi2_bwm1.53: Ehrenfest escaped again! General Ortholion is unconscious and the reinforcements haven't shown up yet...
Omi2_bwm1.54: Kamelio, who was no longer a human being, tried to kill both the general and me, but we survived. Better get out of this cavern as soon as possible.
Omi2_bwm1.55: I got back to the Elm mine dining room. Despite saving the general's life he's not eager to reward me. Maybe I should try again later when we are both more settled.
Omi2_bwm1.56: After arriving back at a safer place, General Ortholion asked me a question. "What is most important to you?" I need to think about it before giving him my reply.
Omi2_bwm1.59: For my bravery, General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of gold and told me to meet him in a couple of days.
Omi2_bwm1.60: For my bravery (and my greediness), General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of...junk. He might pay me better next time if I meet him in some days.
Omi2_bwm1.61: For my bravery (and my lack of honor), General Ortholion rewarded me with a small bag of gold. He may have some news for me in a couple of days.
Omi2_bwm1.62: For my bravery and sense of honor, General Ortholion gave me a beautiful necklace, a symbol of his gratitude towards me. He also told me to come back in a few days, when I should ask him about all the events that have happened.
Omi2_bwm1.63: For my bravery and... ignorance?, General Ortholion gave me a few days to rest and urged me to come back soon after that.
